findings.reason: as written the node cannot satisfy its own gate, and the fix is to add the test to §13's write paths and its done-when (as §16 did for the same test).
findings.text: §13 removes §16's interim metered-lane caveat and requires "the skill-contract tests pass", but `tests/test_skills_load_full_width.py:76` asserts the caveat's exact text (`"metered request still \`awaiting-upstream\` or \`queued\`" in build`) and `:72-75` asserts the build skill's "steer waiting requests with the three queue verbs below" sentence that §13 must reword to name hold and release; that test file is not among §13's write paths, so the node breaks a test it is fenced out of repairing

findings.reason: the derivation as cited cannot produce the section's own fence, so a worker launched from a batch would be blocked or over-scoped, and the plan must either name a parser that captures all path tokens or require explicit write paths for non-Python sections and make the done-when compare against the full sentence rather than a `.py` subset.
findings.text: §28 takes a derived entry's write paths "through the parser `code_review_paths_from_plan` already uses", but that function reads a whole plan, keeps only implementable sections, and returns their union, and its token regex `_PY_PATH_TOKEN` (reckon/crew/plan_review.py:2359-2360) captures `.py` paths alone — so a batch entry that omits write paths is fenced either to every implementable section's modules at once (defeating per-section claims and the batch's scope discipline) or to a `.py`-only subset that drops every `.md` path and the unnamed "new test" the section's done-when requires; §13's sentence carries zero `.py` tokens, so its entry derives no grant at all

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — `_done_when_paragraph` (reckon/crew/plan_review.py:771), `code_review_paths_from_plan` (:2368), `reckon._plan_html.section_prose` (reckon/_plan_html.py:474), `PLAN_REVIEW_HELD_REASON = "plan-review-owed"` (reckon/crew/queue_admission.py:54) and all four skill/AGENTS.md paths resolve; the wiring claim that the build skill, its orchestration reference, `AGENTS.md` and the user-global guidelines already carry the choose-don't-wholesale wording holds (SKILL.md:141-145, AGENTS.md:31-34).
rubric_items.done_when: a finding — §13's done-when requires removing the interim metered-lane caveat and passing the skill tests, but the test that asserts that caveat is outside §13's write paths.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — neither unit asks for a scratchpad path; their gates are pytest and grep runs recorded by the crew run machinery under the run directory, and §28 names no node-local temporary path.
rubric_items.naming: pass — `dispatch_batch.py`, `crew dispatch --batch` and `plan-review-owed` name mechanisms, and no plan label, stage name, ticket number or version tag is carried into a symbol, file or comment.
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — §28 derives a batch entry's write paths through `code_review_paths_from_plan`, which returns a plan-wide union of `.py` tokens only, so the derived fence is both wider than one section and blind to every non-Python write path.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — §13 carries one deliverable (the skills teach the batch load and the steering verbs) and §28 one (a single batch call queues the chosen sections); the caveat removal is the same instruction change, not a second deliverable.
rubric_items.wiring: pass — §28 declares s26 as its upstream, matching its use of §26's per-section readiness, and §13 declares s9–s12, s15, s16 and s28, which covers every mechanism and verb it names; no declared edge points at the wrong node and no cycle is introduced.
